QUANTUM VULNERABLE   Shor's algorithm breaks these outright

  RSA  (4 call sites, 1 in test code)
    key sizes: 1024: 1, 2048: 1, not stated: 2
    Shor's algorithm factors the modulus in polynomial time.
    migrate to: ML-KEM-768 for key establishment, ML-DSA-65 for signatures
      keys.js:17   crypto.createSign('RSA-SHA256').update(data).sign(privateKey);
      keys.js:28   crypto.generateKeyPairSync('rsa', { modulusLength: 2048 });
      keys.js:32   publicEncrypt(publicKey, Buffer.from('secret'));
      ... and 1 more

  ECDH  (2 call sites)
    parameter sets: SECP256R1: 1, SECP384R1: 1
    Shor's algorithm solves the discrete log on the curve.
    migrate to: ML-KEM-768, ideally hybrid X25519+ML-KEM during transition
      keys.js:33   crypto.createECDH('prime256v1');
      module.mjs:6   export const ecdh = () => nodeCrypto.createECDH('secp384r1');

  DH  (1 call site)
    key sizes: 2048: 1
    Shor's algorithm solves the finite-field discrete log.
    migrate to: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203)
      keys.js:34   crypto.createDiffieHellman(2048);

  DSA  (1 call site)
    key sizes: 1024: 1
    Shor's algorithm solves the finite-field discrete log.
    migrate to: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204)
      module.mjs:5   export const keyPair = () => gen('dsa', { modulusLength: 1024 });

  Ed25519  (1 call site)

    Curve448 discrete log falls to Shor's algorithm.

USAGE UNDETERMINED   quantum vulnerable, but signing or key agreement is not visible

  EC  (1 call site)
    parameter sets: SECP256R1: 1
    Shor's algorithm solves the discrete log on the curve. Whether this key signs or agrees keys was not visible to the scanner, and the migration target depends on which.
    migrate to: determine usage before migrating, ML-DSA-65 if signing, ML-KEM-768 if key agreement
      keys.js:29   crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ec', { namedCurve: 'P-256' });


ALREADY BROKEN       weak today, quantum is not the issue

  MD5  (2 call sites)
    Collisions are practical today. Quantum is not the problem here.
    migrate to: SHA-256 or SHA-3, or BLAKE2 for non-compliance use
      keys.js:8   crypto.createHash('md5').update(data);
      module.mjs:4   export const fingerprint = (data) => createHash('md5').update(data).digest('hex');

  SHA-1  (2 call sites)
    Chosen-prefix collisions demonstrated in 2020. Retire it.
    migrate to: SHA-256 or SHA-3
      keys.js:9   digest(LEGACY_HASH).update(data);
      keys.js:11   crypto.createHmac('SHA1', key);

  3DES  (1 call site)
    Sweet32 birthday attacks. Disallowed by NIST for encryption after 2023.
    migrate to: AES-256-GCM
      keys.js:22   crypto.createCipheriv('des-ede3-cbc', key, iv);

  RC4  (1 call site)
    Biased keystream. Prohibited in TLS since RFC 7465.
    migrate to: AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305
      keys.js:24   crypto.createDecipheriv('rc4', key, null);


REVIEW               reduced margin under Grover, usually acceptable

  SHA-256  (3 call sites)
    Grover gives a quadratic speedup only. Still acceptable.
    migrate to: no action needed
      keys.js:10   crypto.createHash('sha256').update(data);
      keys.js:17   crypto.createSign('RSA-SHA256').update(data).sign(privateKey);
      keys.js:18   crypto.sign('sha256', data, privateKey);   // the key decides RSA or EC: only the hash is claimed

  AES  (1 call site)
    key sizes: 256: 1
    Grover halves effective key length. AES-256 stays at 128-bit margin.
    migrate to: AES-256 if currently AES-128
      keys.js:23   crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', key, iv);
